# caapi

```go
import "github.com/effective-security/trustyca/server/service/internal/caapi"
```

Package caapi holds the request handling that the CA service \(server/service/ca, pb.CA\) and the backend service \(server/service/backend, privpb.Backend\) share: the tenant scope of a request and the authorization of the rows it reaches \(Scope\), the precondition refusal of the CA \(HTTP 409 conflict, gRPC FailedPrecondition\), request parsing and the source of the audit events. It is internal to server/service.

```
scope := caapi.NewScope(authorizer, caDb, orgsDb)
orgID, err := scope.Org(ctx, req.OrgID)
if err != nil {
	return nil, err
}
projectID, err := scope.Project(ctx, orgID, req.ProjectID)
```

<a name="PreconditionFailed"></a>
## func [PreconditionFailed](<https://github.com/effective-security/trustyca/blob/main/server/service/internal/caapi/request.go#L26>)

```go
func PreconditionFailed(ctx context.Context, msgFormat string, vals ...any) *httperror.Error
```

PreconditionFailed returns the error of a request that the current state of the org refuses, and that the caller can make pass by changing that state: HTTP 409 Conflict with code "conflict", and gRPC FailedPrecondition. The pinned porto maps FailedPrecondition to HTTP 400, so it is built from the HTTP status and returned unwrapped; a remote backend's refusal is restored by the CA service that forwards to it.

<a name="Scope"></a>
## type [Scope](<https://github.com/effective-security/trustyca/blob/main/server/service/internal/caapi/scope.go#L21-L25>)

Scope resolves the tenant scope of a CA request and authorizes the rows the request reaches, for the CA service and the backend service: the org and the project of the request, and the project of a row found by ID. It reads the CA tables and the orgs only.

<a name="Scope.ListProjects"></a>
### func \(\*Scope\) [ListProjects](<https://github.com/effective-security/trustyca/blob/main/server/service/internal/caapi/scope.go#L174>)

```go
func (s *Scope) ListProjects(ctx context.Context, orgID xdb.ID) ([]uint64, error)
```

ListProjects returns the projects whose rows a list of the org without a project includes, next to the org\-wide rows: nil, every project, for a trusted service caller, an API key and a member with an org\-wide role; otherwise the projects the member has a grant in, since a member with project grants only sees nothing of the other projects \(DESIGN.md section 3.3\). An API key restricted to a project never lists without a project: Project selects its project.

<a name="Scope.Org"></a>
### func \(\*Scope\) [Org](<https://github.com/effective-security/trustyca/blob/main/server/service/internal/caapi/scope.go#L40>)

```go
func (s *Scope) Org(ctx context.Context, reqOrgID string) (xdb.ID, error)
```

Org returns the org of a tenant request. A user or API key token carries the selected org, and an explicit OrgID in the request must match it. A trusted service caller \(RA, CIS, jobs over mTLS\) has no org in its token and names the org explicitly; the org must exist and be active.

<a name="Scope.Project"></a>
### func \(\*Scope\) [Project](<https://github.com/effective-security/trustyca/blob/main/server/service/internal/caapi/scope.go#L75>)

```go
func (s *Scope) Project(ctx context.Context, orgID xdb.ID, reqProjectID string) (xdb.ID, error)
```

Project returns the project of a tenant request, or a zero ID for the org scope. A project of another org or an inactive project is reported as not found, so that project existence is not leaked across orgs.

<a name="Scope.RequestProject"></a>
### func \(\*Scope\) [RequestProject](<https://github.com/effective-security/trustyca/blob/main/server/service/internal/caapi/scope.go#L106>)

```go
func (s *Scope) RequestProject(ctx context.Context, orgID xdb.ID, reqProjectID string) (xdb.ID, error)
```

RequestProject returns the project a mutation names explicitly, verified as Project does, or a zero ID when the request names none: unlike Project it does not default to the project of a restricted API key, since the row's own project is authorized by RowAccess, where the key reads an org\-wide row but may not change it

<a name="Scope.RowAccess"></a>
### func \(\*Scope\) [RowAccess](<https://github.com/effective-security/trustyca/blob/main/server/service/internal/caapi/scope.go#L126>)

```go
func (s *Scope) RowAccess(ctx context.Context, orgID, projectID xdb.ID, method, what string) error
```

RowAccess checks that the caller may call the method on a row of the project of the org, after the interceptor authorized the scope of the request: a row named by its ID can belong to a project the request did not name. A trusted service caller passes. An API key passes when it is org\-wide, or restricted to that project; a key restricted to a project reads an org\-wide row \(zero project\) as the derived org Viewer and may not change it, so it passes only a method that allows Viewer. A user needs one of the roles the method allows at the project, where an org\-wide role is inherited, and at the org for an org\-wide row, which a member with project grants only holds as Viewer \(DESIGN.md section 3.3\). A project the caller cannot read, an inactive project and a project of another org are reported as not found, so that project existence does not leak; a project the caller reads but cannot act on at the method's roles is forbidden.
